source: MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise Matrix (Structured Canonical Dataset)

tactics.name: Reconnaissance
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to gather information they can use to plan future operations.

tactics.name: Resource Development
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to establish resources they can use to support operations.

tactics.name: Initial Access
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to get into your network.

tactics.name: Execution
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to run malicious code.

tactics.name: Persistence
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to maintain their foothold.

tactics.name: Privilege Escalation
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to gain higher-level permissions.

tactics.name: Defense Evasion
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to avoid being detected.

tactics.name: Credential Access
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to steal account names and passwords.

tactics.name: Discovery
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to figure out your environment.

tactics.name: Lateral Movement
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to move through your environment.

tactics.name: Collection
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to gather data of interest to their goal.

tactics.name: Command and Control
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to communicate with compromised systems to control them.

tactics.name: Exfiltration
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to steal data.

tactics.name: Impact
tactics.description: The adversary is trying to manipulate, interrupt, or destroy your systems and data.

techniques.name: Phishing
techniques.description: Adversaries may send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.description: Adversaries may send spearphishing emails with a malicious file attachment.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Link
techniques.description: Adversaries may send spearphishing emails with a malicious link targeting specific victims.

techniques.name: Spearphishing via Service
techniques.description: Adversaries may send spearphishing messages via third-party services.

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to take advantage of a weakness in an Internet-facing computer or program.

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of existing accounts as a means of gaining Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation, or Defense Evasion.

techniques.name: Default Accounts
techniques.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse default credentials.

techniques.name: Domain Accounts
techniques.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of a domain account.

techniques.name: Local Accounts
techniques.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of a local account.

techniques.name: Cloud Accounts
techniques.description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse credentials of a cloud account.

techniques.name: User Execution
techniques.description: An adversary may rely upon specific actions by a user in order to gain execution.

techniques.name: Malicious Link
techniques.description: An adversary may rely upon a user clicking a malicious link to gain execution.

techniques.name: Malicious File
techniques.description: An adversary may rely upon a user opening a malicious file to gain execution.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse command and script interpreters to execute commands, scripts, or binaries.

techniques.name: PowerShell
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution.

techniques.name: Windows Command Shell
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse cmd.exe for execution.

techniques.name: Unix Shell
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse Unix shells (sh, bash, zsh) for execution.

techniques.name: Visual Basic
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse Visual Basic (VBScript or VBA macros) for execution.

techniques.name: JavaScript
techniques.description: Adversaries may abuse JavaScript for execution.

techniques.name: Template Injection
techniques.description: Adversaries may create or modify references within office document templates to execute malicious code.

techniques.name: Masquerading
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to manipulate features of their artifacts to make them appear legitimate.

techniques.name: Right-to-Left Override
techniques.description: Adversaries may use the right-to-left override (RTLO or RLO) character to mask the true file extension of an executable.

techniques.name: Match Legitimate Name or Location
techniques.description: Adversaries may match or approximate legitimate file names or paths to evade defenses.

techniques.name: Double File Extension
techniques.description: Adversaries may use a double file extension to deceive users into executing an unauthorized file.

techniques.name: File Type Ambiguities
techniques.description: Adversaries may exploit file format ambiguities to evade detection while ensuring successful execution.

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to make an executable or file difficult to discover or analyze.

techniques.name: Software Packing
techniques.description: Adversaries may perform software packing to compress, encrypt, or modify an executable payload.

techniques.name: Impair Defenses
techniques.description: Adversaries may maliciously modify defensive tools or configurations.

techniques.name: Brute Force
techniques.description: Adversaries may use brute force techniques to attempt access to accounts when passwords are unknown or when password hashes are obtained.

techniques.name: Password Guessing
techniques.description: Adversaries may systematically guess passwords to authenticate to a specific account.

techniques.name: Password Cracking
techniques.description: Adversaries may use password cracking to recover plain-text credentials from acquired hashes.

techniques.name: Password Spraying
techniques.description: Adversaries may use a single or small list of commonly used passwords against many accounts to avoid account lockouts.

techniques.name: Credential Stuffing
techniques.description: Adversaries may use credentials obtained from past breaches across accounts on other systems.

techniques.name: Input Capture
techniques.description: Adversaries may use methods of capturing user input to obtain credentials or sensitive information.

techniques.name: Web Portal Capture
techniques.description: Adversaries may install or host malicious login portals to capture user credentials.

techniques.name: Unsecured Credentials
techniques.description: Adversaries may search compromised systems to find and obtain insecurely stored credentials.

techniques.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
techniques.description: Adversaries may use alternate authentication material, such as session cookies or tokens, to bypass authentication challenges.

techniques.name: Web Session Cookie
techniques.description: Adversaries may steal and reuse web application session cookies to bypass multifactor authentication.

techniques.name: Modify Authentication Process
techniques.description: Adversaries may modify authentication mechanisms to maintain access or harvest credentials.

techniques.name: Account Manipulation
techniques.description: Adversaries may manipulate accounts to maintain access to victim systems.

techniques.name: Create Account
techniques.description: Adversaries may create an account to maintain access to victim systems.

techniques.name: Account Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of accounts on a system or within an environment.

techniques.name: Local Account
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of local system accounts.

techniques.name: Domain Account
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of domain accounts.

techniques.name: Cloud Account
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of cloud accounts.

techniques.name: File and Directory Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries may enumerate files and directories or search in specific locations.

techniques.name: Network Service Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts.

techniques.name: System Information Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to get detailed information about the operating system and hardware.

techniques.name: Active Scanning
techniques.description: Adversaries may execute active reconnaissance scans to gather information on targets.

techniques.name: Vulnerability Scanning
techniques.description: Adversaries may scan for vulnerabilities on victim systems.

techniques.name: Remote System Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to get a listing of other systems on the network.

techniques.name: Cloud Infrastructure Discovery
techniques.description: Adversaries may attempt to discover cloud infrastructure resources.

techniques.name: Remote Services
techniques.description: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to log into a service that accepts remote connections.

techniques.name: Remote Desktop Protocol
techniques.description: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to log into remote systems using RDP.

techniques.name: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
techniques.description: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to interact with remote SMB shares.

techniques.name: SSH
techniques.description: Adversaries may use Valid Accounts to log into remote machines using SSH.

techniques.name: Automated Collection
techniques.description: Once established within a system, adversaries may leverage automated techniques to collect internal data.

techniques.name: Data from Local System
techniques.description: Adversaries may search local system sources, such as the file system, to find files of interest.

techniques.name: Email Collection
techniques.description: Adversaries may leverage email collection techniques to access emails and attachments.

techniques.name: Local Email Collection
techniques.description: Adversaries may collect email data from local client applications.

techniques.name: Remote Email Collection
techniques.description: Adversaries may collect email data from remote email servers (e.g. Exchange, IMAP).

techniques.name: Email Forwarding Rule
techniques.description: Adversaries may set up email forwarding rules to collect sensitive emails automatically.

techniques.name: Archive Collected Data
techniques.description: An adversary may compress or encrypt data prior to exfiltration.

techniques.name: Data from Information Repositories
techniques.description: Adversaries may leverage information repositories (SharePoint, Confluence) to gather valuable data.

techniques.name: Data from Cloud Storage
techniques.description: Adversaries may access data objects from cloud storage containers.

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol
techniques.description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer protocols to avoid detection/network filtering.

techniques.name: Web Protocols
techniques.description: Adversaries may communicate using application layer web protocols (HTTP, HTTPS) to avoid detection.

techniques.name: DNS
techniques.description: Adversaries may communicate using the Domain Name System (DNS) application layer protocol to avoid detection.

techniques.name: Dynamic Resolution
techniques.description: Adversaries may dynamically establish connections to command and control infrastructure.

techniques.name: Domain Generation Algorithms
techniques.description: Adversaries may make use of Domain Generation Algorithms (DGAs) to dynamically identify destination C2 domains.

techniques.name: Proxy
techniques.description: Adversaries may use a connection proxy to direct network traffic between systems or outside the network.

techniques.name: Multi-hop Proxy
techniques.description: Adversaries may chain together multiple proxies to disguise the source of their traffic.

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.description: Adversaries may transfer tools or other files from an external system into a compromised network.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
techniques.description: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over an existing command and control channel.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
techniques.description: Adversaries may steal data by exfiltrating it over a different protocol than that used for Command and Control.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Unencrypted Non-C2 Protocol
techniques.description: Adversaries may exfiltrate data using an unencrypted network protocol such as FTP, HTTP, or DNS.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
techniques.description: Adversaries may use an existing, legitimate external Web service to exfiltrate data.

techniques.name: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
techniques.description: Adversaries may exfiltrate data to a cloud storage service rather than an adversary-owned server.

techniques.name: Automated Exfiltration
techniques.description: Adversaries may leverage automated capabilities to transfer data out of an enterprise network.

techniques.name: Acquire Infrastructure
techniques.description: Adversaries may buy, lease, or rent infrastructure that can be used during targeting.

techniques.name: Domains
techniques.description: Adversaries may acquire domains that can be used during targeting, including lookalike or typo-squatted domains.

techniques.name: Obtain Capabilities
techniques.description: Adversaries may obtain capabilities such as malware, software tools, or exploits.

techniques.name: Tool: Malware
techniques.description: Adversaries may buy, steal, or download malware to use in operations.

techniques.name: Phishing for Information
techniques.description: Adversaries may send phishing messages to elicit sensitive information directly.

techniques.name: Impersonation
techniques.description: Adversaries may impersonate a trusted entity or brand to deceive users.

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
techniques.description: Adversaries may encrypt data on target systems to interrupt availability.

techniques.name: Endpoint Denial of Service
techniques.description: Adversaries may perform endpoint denial of service attacks to degrade or block service availability.

techniques.name: Application Exhaustion Flood
techniques.description: Adversaries may flood applications with requests to exhaust resources and deny service.

techniques.name: PowerShell (Deprecated)
techniques.description: PowerShell execution technique (revoked by T1059.001 in ATT&CK Enterprise v7+).

techniques.name: Scripting (Deprecated)
techniques.description: Generic scripting technique (revoked by T1059 in ATT&CK Enterprise v7+).
